input: nums is a list of n positive integers in [1,1000000], with 0 <= n <= 10000. Inputs with fewer than three entries are an explicit extension. Integer inputs are plain int values excluding bool. Containers are ordinary lists and strings are ordinary str values, without subclasses or overloaded behavior. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not dynamically validated. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The largest perimeter of any nondegenerate triangle formed from three distinct input occurrences, or 0 if none exists. Equal-valued occurrences may be used separately; a zero-area triangle is not valid.
mutation_aliasing: Only a fresh copy is sorted; caller values and ordering remain unchanged. No triangle or mutated array is returned. The Solution instance retains no state; separate calls share no mutable result state.
numeric: Every pair sum is at most 2000000 and every three-side perimeter at most 3000000. Comparator differences are within [-999999,999999]. Indices and all arithmetic intermediates are exact safe integers.
complexity: After sorting, O(n+1) descending work checks consecutive triples from the largest side down. If its two largest possible smaller sides fail the strict triangle inequality, no triangle with that largest side can succeed; the first success maximizes perimeter. Python copied sorting adds O(n*log(n+1)+1) time and O(n+1) auxiliary space.
